title: Multimodal Aligned Semantic Knowledge for Unpaired Image-text Matching
claim: Prior methods map words to visual prototypes without handling out-of-distribution words; ours bridges modalities via word embeddings to align semantic knowledge.
layout: 2 panels, left-to-right, (a) prior vs (b) ours, 3D axes with colored points
description: A two-panel figure with captions (a) 'Existing unpaired image-text matching' and (b) 'Multimodal aligned semantic knowledge'. Panel (a) flows from raw photos through object detection into region representations, then a 3D visual prototype space with colored squares (yellow, green, red) and star prototypes. Words (dog, cat marked OOD with a question mark, women, peak) sit on the right, linked by alignment lines, with tokenized caption text further right. The OOD word 'cat' has no matching prototype. Panel (b) has two rounded boxes. Left is the visual prototype space, where feature regularization produces region representations that are aggregated into weighted prototypes. Right is the word embedding space, where dog, cat, women and peak are linked by semantic-similarity triangles. Curved arrows labeled v = f⁻¹(w) and w = f(v) show cross-modal semantic alignment, and a blue star marks the cat prototype. Color-coded words and points tie the elements together.
caption: Comparison between existing matching paradigms and our proposed unpaired framework.
abstract: While existing approaches address unpaired image-text matching by constructing cross-modal aligned knowledge, they often fail to identify semantically corresponding visual representations for Out-of-Distribution (OOD) words. Moreover, the distributional variance of visual representations associated with different words varies significantly, which negatively impacts matching accuracy. To address these issues, we propose a novel method namely Multimodal Aligned Semantic Knowledge (MASK), which leverages word embeddings as bridges to associate words with their corresponding prototypes, thereby enabling semantic knowledge alignment between the image and text modalities. For OOD words, the representative prototypes are constructed by leveraging the semantic relationships encoded in word embeddings. Beyond that, we introduce a prototype consistency contrastive loss to structurally regularize the feature space, effectively mitigating the adverse effects of variance. Experimental results on the Flickr30K and MSCOCO datasets demonstrate that MASK achieves superior performance in unpaired matching.
